title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G is a group scheme locally of finite presentation over a scheme S. The handwritten condition on the previous page appears to be that S is reduced ('génériquement réduit' is uncertain). g is a section of G. The previous page studied GL_4 over a DVR A of residue characteristic 2. There X = log g is nilpotent with X^4 = 0, exp(X) is integral, and the question was whether the individual terms X^2/2 and X^3/6 are then integral. Grothendieck saw that a counterexample or a theorem was needed. On this page he states a 'Théorème (!)':

Claim. g is generically unipotent (g_eta is unipotent at the generic points) if and only if there exist an integer n > 0 and a homomorphism of group schemes phi: G_a -> G over S with phi(1) = g^n.

The image reads G_a, not G_m, and the case analysis requires G_a.

Sufficiency is trivial: the image of G_a is unipotent, so g^n is generically unipotent, hence so is g.

For necessity he reduces to S reduced and integral, with generic point eta. He says the reduction from reduced to integral should follow by easy dévissages he does not want to write out.

(a) char k(eta) = p > 0. A unipotent element over a field of characteristic p has finite (p-power) order, so g_eta^n = 1. He concludes g^n = 1 on S and takes phi trivial.

(b) char k(eta) = 0. Let phi_{1,eta}: G_{a,eta} -> G_eta be the unique homomorphism with phi_{1,eta}(1) = g_eta. This is the exponential, lambda -> g_eta^lambda = exp(lambda log g_eta). Let U be its 'open set of definition', the largest open set to which it extends. Put phi_{n,eta}(lambda) = phi_{1,eta}(n lambda), i.e. g^{n lambda}, with domain U_n. Then phi_n(1) = g^n on U_n.

The next page notes that n | n' implies U_n ⊂ U_{n'}. One must show that the union of the U_n is S. This reduces to S local with phi_1 defined on the punctured spectrum, and then to a Lemma: if a generic exponential has phi(1) extending, then for some n the map lambda -> phi(n lambda) extends. He then tests only G = GL_N with S regular of dimension 1.

What this serves: constructing and characterising generically unipotent sections in mixed characteristic. The goal is to replace the hard n = 1 integrality question of (12 bis) by the softer statement 'up to replacing g by g^n'. Context: Longue Marche sequel, around p. 653.

Check for GL_N (Z-flat A, g integral with (g-1)^N = 0). We have g^{n lambda} = sum_{k<N} binom(n lambda, k) (g-1)^k. Since k! n^k-type divisibility makes binom(n lambda, k) lie in Z[lambda] for k < N when, e.g., n = (N-1)!^? suffices (n divisible by enough of each p ≤ N-1, e.g. n = ((N-1)!)^2 works generously), the lemma holds with n independent of A. For flat closed subgroups of GL_N, the case b) lemma then follows by taking schematic closures. So the strategy is sound in the affine flat case.
errors: Case (a): from g_eta^n = 1 he concludes g^n = 1 on all of S. This uses that G is separated over S (with S reduced). G is only assumed locally of finite presentation, and for non-separated G two sections can agree generically without being equal. The separatedness hypothesis is missing or tacit.

Case (b) in general (non-affine, non-flat or non-separated G) also implicitly needs uniqueness of extensions, and an embedding into GL_N to reduce to the matrix case. Neither is available in the stated generality. Grothendieck himself retreats to GL_N over a dimension-1 regular base on the next page.
The reduction from reduced to integral S is waved away ('dévissages faciles'), not done.

In the 'Théorème' some reducedness or flatness hypothesis on S is essential; as a slip-free statement for arbitrary S it would fail on non-reduced bases (nilpotent sections). Grothendieck does impose 'S réduit'.

ideas.what: Characterisation: a section g is generically unipotent iff some power g^n is phi(1) for a homomorphism phi: G_a -> G over the reduced base S.
ideas.modern_name: Exponential / one-parameter additive subgroups through unipotent elements over a mixed-characteristic base (integral exponentials, 'exponential type' homomorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Over fields: classical (char 0 exponential; Springer, Seitz, Serre on exponentiation/saturation in char p). Over Z or a DVR: McNinch, Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran style results for reductive groups. Unsure that the general group-scheme statement appears anywhere.
ideas.where_published: Not known in SGA 3 in this form (Exp. XVII treats unipotent groups over fields)

ideas.what: Unipotent elements in characteristic p have finite p-power order, so case (a) is trivial with phi trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Unipotent elements are p-torsion in char p

ideas.what: Domain-of-definition ('ouvert de définition') argument: the open sets U_n where g^{n lambda} extends increase with divisibility, and one shows their union is S, reducing to a Hartogs/codimension-1 problem.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of homomorphisms from the generic fibre / Weil extension-type argument; p-power rescaling of integral exponentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil extension theorem (for rational maps into group schemes), Néron-model techniques (BLR)

missed.claim: Grothendieck states, with '(!)', a general criterion for generically unipotent sections of a group scheme locally of finite presentation over a reduced base: g^n = phi(1) for a homomorphism G_a -> G. He verifies it only as a 'test décisif' for GL_N over a regular 1-dimensional base. The general statement, especially for non-affine, non-flat or non-separated G, is left open, and I do not know a published general version.
missed.quote: Pour que g soit génériquement unipotent, il faut et il suffit qu'il existe un entier n>0, et un homomorphisme de schémas en groupes φ: G_a → G, tel qu'on ait φ(1) = g^n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral exponentials and G_a-actions over Z or Z_p matter in mixed-characteristic representation theory and in Bruhat–Tits and Néron models. A clean criterion, with exact hypotheses (separatedness, flatness) and counterexamples, is a small but genuine gap. For affine flat G it reduces to the easy GL_N case.

deep.surprise_reason: A tidy, apparently unpublished formulation for general group schemes, but mathematically close to routine. Case (a) is classical, and case (b) for affine flat G reduces to the elementary GL_N computation via binomial polynomials. The open part is mainly the non-affine or non-separated generality, which Grothendieck himself declines to pursue.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 of the page and (14): the group is G_a ('φ: G_a → G', 'φ_{1η}: G_{a,η} → G_η'), not G_m.
'Car[?] où g_η est >0[?]' should read 'Cas où car η > 0' (residue characteristic of the generic point positive).
'Cas où g est d'ordre[?] nulle[?]' should read 'Cas où η de car. nulle' (characteristic zero at the generic point).
'φ_{nη}(λ) = λ^n = φ_{1η}(nλ)' is better read as 'φ_{nη}(λ) = φ_{1η}(nλ)', i.e. g^{nλ}; the multiplicative 'λ^n' is a misreading or a slip.
'Pour simplifier, on va mener[?] supposer S réduit et intègre' should read roughly 'on va (même) supposer S réduit et intègre'.
Line before (a): likely 'Je vais donc examiner le cas S réduit intègre, et génériquement...' (incomplete), not 'géométriquement'.
